properties.name: A defect sweep builds its network a fixed number of times, never once per candidate
properties.statement:
`detect_defects` shall build the design/operational network **no more than 4 times per call, independent of how many single-point-of-failure candidates it examines**.

THE DERIVATION, and it is a statement about what ought to be true rather than a round number. The question the sweep asks of each candidate is "does removing THIS node split off a non-trivial component?" The graph DOES NOT CHANGE between candidates — only which node is masked. So the network has to be constructed once and interrogated N times; nothing about the question requires reconstructing it per candidate. Four is what the sweep legitimately needs: a design network for the structural rules, one for the sweep scope, one operational network for the articulation scan, and one baseline component count. A fifth would need an argument; a per-candidate one cannot have one.

MEASURED BEFORE THE BUDGET WAS WRITTEN, 2026-08-21, on reflow2's own design (2871 nodes) with the in-memory backend in a debug build:

  detect_defects                  71.5s
    sweep_scope                   15.1s
    all_defects                   56.3s
      detect_structural_defects   44.5s   <- 62% of the whole
  operational_network(None) x1   401ms    (329 nodes)
  articulation_points            191µs    -> 56 candidates
  is_single_point_of_failure x1  878ms    = TWO network builds

  56 candidates x 878ms = 49s, which IS detect_structural_defects.

So the sweep currently builds ~115 networks per call where 4 would do. Each build calls `outgoing` once per included node — 329 of them — so this is roughly **37,000 store reads spent re-deriving a graph that never changed**. Of those builds, HALF are the `operational_network(None)` baseline, which is byte-identical on every one of the 56 iterations.

WHY BUILDS AND NOT SECONDS. A count is what the code controls and what survives a loaded machine; a duration assertion in a parallel suite measures contention, and the standing response is to raise the threshold until it stops complaining, which retires the gate without anybody deciding to. It is also the quantity that carries across backends, which seconds do not.

⚠️ HONEST LIMITS. The breakdown above is the in-memory backend in a debug build, which is NOT what users run. The RATIO is the transferable part; on RocksDB with a release binary the same call measures 10.3s. Two candidate counts (56 here) is one design's shape, and a design with more subsystems has more candidates and pays more — which is exactly what the "independent of candidates" clause exists to stop.

📌 WHAT THIS IS FOR, so the number is not mistaken for tidiness: `detect_defects` is paid by `loop_status` and, through the loop hint, by `open_questions` — the first call every session makes, measured at 11.7s of which 10.3 is this. The sweep is not a background chore; it is on the critical path of saying hello.
